preamble: Fortition of the palatal glide /j/ to the voiced retroflex fricative /ʐ/ (Mandarin r, realized [ʐ] ~ [ɻ]). In Mandarin a small group of Middle Chinese yi-initial (以母, Baxter y-) characters before rounded finals irregularly took the r- initial that normally continues the Middle Chinese palatal nasal (日母): 容 yowng > róng (also the phonetic series 蓉, 溶), 融 yuwng > róng, 銳 ywejH > ruì. Most yi-initial words regularly give Mandarin y- or zero (庸 yōng), so the change is sporadic and lexically restricted.

examples.note: Wiktionary transcribes the initial as [ɻ] (/ɻʊŋ³⁵/); Wikipedia's Standard Chinese phonology gives the phoneme as /ʐ/ with [ɻ] as a free variant.

examples.from: Middle Chinese 蓉 yowng 'lotus paste; hibiscus (in 芙蓉)'

examples.note: Irregular: the regular reflex of the yi-initial is Mandarin y-/zero.
Same treatment as 銳 ywejH, which shares the yi-initial and the final.

sources: Baxter, W. H. (1992). A Handbook of Old Chinese Phonology. Mouton de Gruyter. https://doi.org/10.1515/9783110857085
